title: REMM Project coordinated intensive courses in Mozambique and Madagascar
content:
TreesForDev project personnel, Marketta Vuola and Ossi Ollinaho also work with the REMM project. Many of the themes of the REMM project overlap with the TreesForDev project. 

Mozambique

The first training was organized at the Eduardo Mondlane University’s (UEM) Faculty of Agronomy and Forestry Engineering (FAEF) between August 31 and September 5, 2026. The training focused on forest restoration in miombo forest and mangroves and it gathered together professors, graduate students, researchers, and technicians from non-governmental organizations, as well as representatives of public and private institutions. The course aimed to strengthen the scientific, methodological, and practical skills of the participants for understanding the processes of ecosystem degradation and restoration, contributing to the training of specialists capable of responding to the challenges associated with climate change and biodiversity loss.

title: Learnings from the Urban Mushroom Upcycling Operations pilot
content:
At first, a brewery and a mushroom farm might not seem to have much in common. One produces beer. The other grows fungi.

But in Viikki, University of Helsinki students tested what happens when the two are connected and when the mycelia – i.e. the mushroom spawn – becomes part of an even bigger loop.

From May to September 2026, a group of University of Helsinki students calling themselves the Shroomhead crew (Milla Tammivuori, Volter Kaitila, Silver De Vries, Sanni Taba and Amanda Tikkanen) took part in the Urban Mushroom Upcycling Operations Pilot, an experiment in local food production, circular bioeconomy and urban upcycling.

Coordinated by the Viikki Food Design Factory, this pilot brought together students, university researchers and local companies, Helsieni and CoolHead Brew. Together, they explored whether mushroom cultivation, food production and material experimentation could be interconnected into a local, urban circular operation.

The idea is simple. Grow mushrooms locally. Eat them locally. Then ask what can be done with what is left.

title: Call for talks and posters: HELDIG Summit 2026 Methodological encounters
content:
We are gathering speakers and poster proposals for the next HELDIG Summit that aims to provide a snapshot of digital research in SSH today. To bring about discussion, we are planning three themes: digital history, digital social sciences and digital heritage. We invite you to contribute to this event with a 5 minute flash-talk or poster from recent or ongoing project(s). The Summit is a good opportunity to give visibility to your latest research and tools, get inspired by methodological innovations in similar fields, and make new connections. 

The HELDIG Summit brings together social sciences and humanities in a day that takes a snapshot at the state of the art in digital research. This year, we bring discussion around methodological and infrastructure encounters beyond disciplines. What challenges in data processing new methods enable us to overcome? How to maintain and adapt our research tools to fast-changing technological landscape? How to target the use of AI responsibly in the research cycle? 

The Summit will take place on December 4 (we aim for a full-day 10:00-18:00), after which there will be a cocktail reception.

title: Maisteriohjelman opinnot käynnistyivät orientaatioviikolla Viikin kampuksella
content:
The first students of the Master's Programme in Technologies for Sustainable Use of Renewable Resources arrived in Viikki on Monday and were greeted by student tutors. On Tuesday, the Faculty of Agriculture and Forestry held its welcome event for all incoming master's students.

Students had the chance to get to know one another and familiarise themselves with the campus and induction activities.

Wednesday’s programme day began with morning coffee at the EE-building, where staff presented the programme’s specialisation modules, the structure of the studies and features such as field periods and cooperation with companies. The day also included work on course selections and an introduction to the Sisu system. In the afternoon, attendees networked with faculty and programme staff at the Forest Sciences Building; snacks and Finnish treats were provided.

Towards the end of the orientation week there was a Check‑in event for international students at the City Centre Campus, offering an introduction to various student organisations, Finnish student life and practical matters for those arriving in Finland.
